text:
Sam: quick heads-up — competitor launched a low-cost, low-latency "EdgeLite" tier this morning. Need a 10m sync: do we build parity (match feature) or lean into differentiation (reliability + clear quality tiers)?
Maria: saw it. their approach looks like aggressive quant + tiny model + aggressive caching. We can hit latency but unit cost might not improve without new quant profiles.
Derek: UX concern — shipping a lower-fidelity tier without clear labeling will confuse customers. We need explicit opt-in and quality indicators.
Anita: sales feedback: two pilot customers asked for a cheaper option last week. They'll convert if margin and SLA are clear.
Sam: proposed plan: short workstream with 3 deliverables — 1) spec for a parity-lite beta (opt-in only), 2) differentiation checklist (SLOs, evals, rollback), 3) rollout gating criteria. Quick canary 2 weeks.
Maria: rough estimate: 3 sprints to add quant profiles + autoscale rules + cost telemetry. Beta with feature flag in ~6 weeks if prioritized.
Derek: mockups: label variant as "Cost-Optimized — lower fidelity" and show a tooltip that links to examples + expected failure modes. Also add an explicit consent checkbox for production traffic.
Anita: propose beta customers: AcmeRetail, BetaFin, and GoodApps — they signed NDAs and will help test QoE. Sales can commit to pilot terms if canary metrics look good.
Sam: gating thresholds (proposal): p95 latency < 120ms, cost reduction >= 35%, and eval quality delta <= 15% on priority prompt set. If any gate fails, automatic fallback to standard tier.
Maria: will sync with infra about kernel/quant tradeoffs and open a PR for a rollout policy today.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary config created — canary-window=14d, sample=2%, auto-rollback=true
Sam: thanks. I'll update the roadmap board: mark parity-lite as "opt-in beta" and add follow-up ticket for differentiation workstream. Ping me if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
